name: Anyte
bio: Anyte of Tegea in Arcadia, an early third-century BC poet, wrote epitaphs, dedications and small scenes of country life, and was one of the women whom Meleager honoured in his Garland.
The epigrams here are the ones that Paton's first volume ascribes to her.

poems.title: Book VI, 123
poems.author: Anyte
poems.text: Stand here, thou murderous spear, no longer drip from thy brazen barb the dismal blood of foes; but resting in the high marble house of Athene, announce the bravery of Cretan Echecratidas.

poems.title: Book VI, 153
poems.author: Anyte
poems.text: The cauldron would hold an ox; the dedicator is Cleobotus, the son of Eriaspidas ; his city is spacious Tegea. The gift is made to Athene; the artist is Aristoteles of Cleitor, who bears the same name as his father.

poems.title: Book VI, 312
poems.author: Anyte
poems.text: The children, billy-goat, have put purple reins on you and a muzzle on your bearded face, and they train you to race like a horse round the god’s temple that he may look on their childish joy.
